items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers are sounding the alarm related to an active campaign in which unknown threat actors are abusing a compromised Microsoft 365 (M365) credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) to gain unauthorized access to customers' M365 environments. items.title: Pipecat: Public exposure of Pipecat’s development runner can allow unauthenticated bot session creation
items.summary: Pipecat’s built-in development runner exposes endpoints that create bot sessions and, for the Daily transport, paid Daily rooms. These development endpoints intentionally do not authenticate callers. The runner binds to localhost by default and is designed exclusively for local development. It is not built or supported as a production server. Exploitation therefore requires an operator to deliberately make the development runner reachable from an untrusted network, such as by setting --host 0.0.

A user holding the copy permission could copy a file denied by the filters to a permitted name and then read it. items.title: Claude Code: Plugin Hash Pin Bypass Allows Bypass of Hash Pinning
items.summary: The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using `git checkout` without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker controlling a plugin's upstream repository could create a branch named identically to the pinned 40-character SHA, causing the checkout to silently resolve to the attacker's branch tip instead of the reviewed commit, resulting in attacker-controlled code being installed bypassing the pinned hash.

There is no current-password re-prompt and the routes are explicitly registered **outside** the `RequireSecureSession()` group. items.title: Nginx UI: MCP `nginx_config_add` Bypasses Directive Validation — Authenticated RCE
items.summary: ### Summary The MCP tool `nginx_config_add` writes nginx configuration files to disk and triggers an nginx reload without calling `config.ValidateConfigFile`. The identical flow in the REST API (`POST /api/configs`) does call that function and correctly rejects dangerous directives. An authenticated attacker can exploit this gap to write config files containing any blocked directive (`perl`, `js_import`, `load_module`, `user root`, etc.), bypassing nginx-ui's entire security layer. items.title: Nginx UI: MCP nginx_config_add skips config directive validation → authenticated nginx directive injection (RCE on the official image)
items.summary: ## Summary `internal/config/validation.go` (`ValidateConfigFile`) is a security control that blocks dangerous nginx directives — `js_*`, `perl_*`, `load_module` of the njs/perl modules, and `user root`. items.summary: ## Summary Nginx UI validates `backup_path` and `storage_path` against the administrator-defined `backup.GrantedAccessPath` boundary, but the final auto-backup output filename is built from the user-controlled auto-backup `name` without stripping path separators or `..` components. An authenticated user who can create or modify an auto-backup task can set a name such as `task/../../../escaped`. items.summary: ## Summary The regular HTTP configuration API rejects restricted Nginx directives such as `load_module`, `js_import`, and `js_content`. items.title: Junrar: RarVM VM_JMP maxOpCount bypass causes infinite CPU loop during RAR4 extraction
items.summary: ### Summary Junrar's RAR virtual machine can be forced into a deterministic infinite loop while extracting a crafted RAR4 archive. items.title: GitHub CLI allows attestation verification bypass through unescaped regex metacharacters
items.summary: ### Summary A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI that could allow attestation verification bypass when using `gh attestation verify` with `--signer-repo` or `--signer-workflow` flags. GitHub CLI builds the certificate matcher from these flag values without escaping regex metacharacters, so a repository or workflow name is treated as a regular expression rather than a literal string. items.title: GitHub CLI allows path traversal through unescaped request URL components
items.summary: ### Summary A path traversal vulnerability has been identified in the GitHub CLI where some HTTP request URLs, REST API calls in particular, were built without properly escaping their variable path components. items.title: GitHub CLI partially discloses authentication tokens in `gh auth status` output
items.summary: ### Summary A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI where `gh auth status` could potentially print a portion of the authentication token in plaintext, depending on the lexical structure of the token. Affected users: - Authenticated users who ran `gh auth status` (without the `--show-token` flag) with a token type whose format contains an underscore after the prefix.
